source.original_title: 05/08/2026 - Kamal Mohammed & Harry Edmonds KFS- Kettlebell Body Game Plan Session
source.display_title: 05/08/2026 - Kamal Mohammed & Harry Edmonds KFS- Kettlebell Body Game Plan Session — Follow Up

setter.name: Kim Forbes-Sobers
setter.evidence: You spoke with Kim, didn't you, I think? Yeah. On Zoom? Yeah, Kim, yeah

prospect.name: Kamal Mohammed
prospect.location: Chicago, Illinois, USA; originally from Sheffield, UK
prospect.occupation: Convenience store owner, looking to expand into other businesses
prospect.family_status: Married eight years; wife had a baby about a year ago and is currently travelling in New York
prospect.training_background: Essentially untrained. Boxed at 17-18, roughly twelve to thirteen years ago, which he describes as the best shape he has been in. Has been to a gym for about a week total in his life and has done no sport for ten-plus years. Self-reported weight 72kg, up from a lifetime baseline of 60kg and a recent peak of 75-77kg, which he attributes to quitting smoking. No kettlebell experience.
prospect.medical: Long-term smoker who recently quit. Reports poor posture ('even when I sit down, I'd be bending down') and self-described back trouble severe enough that he expects injury on starting: 'my back. feel like if I start training now, I'll pull a muscle or something. That's how bad it is.' No diagnosis, no clinician mentioned. Height not established. Wife is approximately one year postpartum.

signals: Explicitly wants a former self back — boxing at 17-18 was 'probably the time I was in best shape'
Visible regret and shame: 'I just feel disgusting, be honest... just looking at yourself, you don't feel right'
Eight years of unkept promises to his wife: 'I've been telling my wife, oh, I'm gonna go to the gym... she always takes the piss out of me'
Counter-signal: he has never trained systematically at all, so he is closer to a first-timer than a classic rebuilder — the lost ground is a lifetime baseline weight, not a lost fitness base

goals.text: Get shredded — a six-pack and an athletic build, big but ripped rather than just bulky
Lose the weight he has gained since quitting smoking, back toward his lifetime baseline
Build muscle at the same time as losing fat
Rebuild stamina lost to years of smoking and inactivity
Start looking after himself now at 30 so he does not face illness and back pain later
Know exactly what to do and eat, on a proper routine, rather than guessing

pains.text: Completely clueless about training and nutrition — 'Not knowing what to do. I'm clueless. Completely.'
Feels disgusting and wrong looking at himself since gaining weight
Eight years of telling his wife he will start and never doing it; she mocks him for it
Self-described bad back and expectation of injuring himself if he starts training
No stamina after years of smoking and total inactivity
Describes himself as lazy and dependent on motivation that never arrives
Overwhelmed by the number of variables — food, rest, training, form, weight

objections.raw_quote: They even knew what about that thing he uses, the kettlebell, whatever it is, so to see if you can actually make crazy progress and build muscle, get ripped and all that, just by doing that kind of training, that was like...
objections.rep_response: Used himself and Trevor as proof — two to three years of kettlebells only, shared before and after photographs of his own three-month transformation on screen, and positioned the outcome as a fighter physique.

objections.raw_quote: It's called FLF Performance Center. It's, it's, man, it's crazy. Like, every training, it's like, wow, like, how is that even possible in 12 weeks?
objections.rep_response: Did not address the competitor directly. Reframed the timeframe instead — argued a 12-week route could reach 60kg but with no muscle gained, and that six months is required to lose fat and add muscle simultaneously. The prospect later self-disqualified the competitor because it is in-person and in England.

objections.raw_quote: That's what I'm saying, I need to, it can't be today because I need to go to the bank and stuff, that's what it is.
objections.rep_response: Offered to take a small deposit instead, then pushed for $100 on a credit card to start the process. The prospect deflected to checking the time and proposed messaging the next day; the rep accepted and booked a second Zoom rather than pressing further.

offer.payment_plan_terms: No structured instalment plan was defined. When the prospect could not pay, the rep improvised a deposit: 'we can just take a small deposit, that's fine... then do the rest', then narrowed it to 'Do you not have like a hundred bucks to put down as a deposit in your bank? From a credit card account'. No terms for the remaining $5,900 were ever discussed.

evidence: No payment taken and no payment link sent — the rep demonstrated the Stripe form on screen using a dummy entry only
Prospect deferred: 'I'll just message you tomorrow, and I'll go to the bank now, and then I'll message you tomorrow, and we'll take care of it then.'
A second Zoom was booked for the following day at 1pm and the invite was confirmed as received in the prospect's inbox
Strong verbal intent throughout — 'You sure you're all in, brother?' answered 'No, no, I'm all in, man. Hard enough.'

Counter-evidence for a stronger reading: an onboarding slot with Trevor was tentatively named for Tuesday 2pm and met with 'Yeah, that's cool', but it was left tangled in a timezone disagreement and was never confirmed as booked
Prospect declined even a $100 credit-card deposit, which is the strongest available counter-signal to his stated commitment
outcome.next_step: Second Zoom the following day at 1pm Central after the prospect visits the bank; a follow-up call on 2026-05-09 exists in this batch.

notable.note: The rep volunteered that the company will help mischaracterise the coaching fee as a deductible business expense, and cited having done it for a client the previous day. He also committed the prospect's approximately one-year-postpartum wife into the programme's diet and training with no assessment, no clinician question and no discussion of scope or price. Separately, both parties disparaged American customers on the recording, the rep using an ableist slur. Baseline discovery was almost entirely skipped: no health conditions, no injuries, no current diet, no sleep, no energy.

quality.notes: Severe and sustained. Long passages are fully inverted — the entire coaching explanation from roughly 00:12:26 to 00:14:00 is attributed to the prospect, including 'You'll be able to get to 60 kilo in 12 weeks, but you won't put on any muscle', which is unambiguously the rep. The same inversion recurs at 00:02:56, 00:17:08 and 00:24:53. Role was read from content throughout.
